newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Lux sees "tens of billions" in budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Czech Lux sees "tens of billions" in budget cuts.

text.p: Czech Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux said on Thursday that the ruling coalition's new austerity programme would comprise additional budget cuts in the total volume of "tens of billions of crowns".

"On the basis of an analysis I have at my disposal, it is apparent that the cuts will be in the (amount) of tens of billions of crowns," Lux told a news conference, adding that approval in parliament would be necessary.

The budget cuts, which were announced as part of a new government austerity programme hammered out by the ruling coalition on Wednesday but not detailed, would come on top of the 25.5 billion crowns in spending cuts already announced on April 16 as part of a prior austerity programme.
Lux added that the economic situation combined with the plan issued on Wednesday by the coalition would mean an additional three to four percentage points of inflation.
Inflation was 6.7 percent, year-in-year, in April.

Lux, who is the chairman of the junior Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL) in the coalition and is the agriculture minister, said the situation would also lead unemployment to rise to about five to six percent over the next year.
